Sample Name: Consultation for Foot Pain and Prostate Cancer Questions
Description: Evaluation of lower-extremity pain and paresthesias, questions about previously reported prostate cancer, and a recent episode of chest discomfort.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: The patient presents with intermittent pain in the feet and legs, including numbness and tingling, and concern about the information he has received regarding a prostate cancer diagnosis or prostate testing at another facility. He is unsure what treatment, including radiation or surgery, may be planned, and seeks clarification. Much of his prior evaluation occurred at another medical center, and those records are not available during this encounter. He also recounts an episode of chest pain with sweating and arm symptoms lasting several minutes, without current recurrent pain. Cigarette consumption has decreased from previously heavy use but continues. He reports transient tingling and weakness in the arms during another episode.
EXAMINATION: Routine cardiopulmonary, neurologic, and lower-extremity examination was performed; no definitive etiology of the leg symptoms was established. An EKG was arranged because of recent chest pain.
IMPRESSION AND PLAN:
1. Reported prostate cancer or abnormal prostate testing. Definitive findings and stage cannot be confirmed from the current information. Follow up with the treating urologists at the original facility to review records, prognosis, and available treatments before making decisions.
2. Distal foot pain and paresthesias. Recommend evaluation of thyroid function, iron studies, and relevant vitamin deficiencies; written suggested tests provided for completion with his usual care team.
3. Recent chest pain with diaphoresis and arm symptoms. Obtain EKG and review prior cardiac studies. Seek emergency assessment promptly for recurrence; additional stress testing may be necessary depending on prior workup and symptoms.
4. Encouraged coordinated care at the facility where the diagnostic records are held; follow-up at this clinic remains available.
